§21.1 Tick to order and learning — step 7 ('previous package remains rollback-ready')

verification.check: A new package is activated and the network is then cut. A rollback command restores the previous package at the next epoch boundary with no download, and decisions after that carry the previous package's id.

notes: Merges two raw G p6 items and G p20 step 7, and reuses the atomic swap of REFLEX-064. The blueprint does not say who may order a rollback or whether the node may roll back on its own. P1 because the full package lifecycle is GCP Phase 8, though the rollback path costs little once REFLEX-064 exists.

title: Exposure narrows progressively while dependencies stay lost
statement: While running degraded, the cell must narrow its exposure progressively, following local policy, as its envelope, package and other inputs age.
rationale: An envelope issued an hour ago describes an hour-old market, and trading it at full size treats stale authority as fresh. Narrowing turns growing ignorance into smaller positions.

sources.section: §6 Regional Reflex Cell — Degraded mode bullet ('progressively narrows exposure according to local policy')

verification.check: With every central dependency cut, the cell's sizing multiplier falls in steps as each input crosses its staleness threshold. Orders placed later in the outage are no larger than the narrowed limit allows.

notes: Merges two raw G p6 items. In-tree, Cell::narrowing(now) derives a DegradationState whose sizing multiplier narrows as capabilities move from Fresh to Stale to Unavailable. It is published as qip_edge_capability_freshness and qip_edge_sizing_multiplier (§6.2 of the earlier spec).

title: The cell halts when its freshness limits expire
statement: When its freshness limits expire, a degraded cell must exit or halt. It must stop taking new risk rather than keep trading under an envelope it can no longer renew.
rationale: Trading under a stale envelope is justified only for a bounded time. Beyond that the cell would be trading capital nobody has re-granted, on risk nobody has re-assessed, and the fail-closed default is to stop.

sources.section: §6 Regional Reflex Cell — Degraded mode bullet ('then exits/halts if freshness limits expire')

verification.check: With every central dependency cut, once the envelope's freshness limit passes, the cell places no new risk-increasing orders, withdraws its resting orders and reports halted. It resumes only when a fresh, verified envelope arrives.

notes: Merges two raw G p6 items; the second stresses that the non-halting behaviour of REFLEX-052 ends here. 'Exits/halts' could mean flattening positions or stopping the process. The check requires the fail-closed minimum (no new risk, resting orders withdrawn) and leaves flattening to local policy. In-tree, halts come from the kill switch, from policy and from a polled flag (qip_edge_halted{source}), and the Cell withdraws resting orders on a halt (qip_edge_orders_mass_cancelled_total). It remains to be checked whether freshness expiry triggers a halt or only narrows the sizing multiplier.

title: A Reflex process or VM failure is contained to its shard
statement: When a Reflex process or VM fails, only that shard's active venue connections may be lost. Other shards, in the same region or elsewhere, must keep trading.
rationale: Sharding exists to bound the blast radius. If one failure takes down other shards, they were sharing something they should not have been.

sources.section: §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Reflex process/VM row ('active venue connection lost only for that shard')

verification.check: Killing one shard's process, and then its VM, leaves every other shard's venue sessions connected and its decisions uninterrupted. Only the killed shard reports a lost session.

notes: Split from the G p15 row; its promotion clause is REFLEX-060 and its recovery-target clause REFLEX-069. Removed LIVE_CAPITAL. P1 because containment needs more than one shard, which comes after the single-shard Phase 1 cell.

title: Reflex recovery targets are measured per venue and never promised as zero-gap
statement: Reflex failover recovery time must be measured and reported for each venue, and must never be promised as zero-gap.
rationale: Venues differ in how fast a session can be re-established after failover. An unmeasured recovery promise is a false statement that a risk desk will plan around.

sources.section: §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Reflex process/VM row ('Measure target per venue; do not promise zero-gap failover')

verification.check: A scheduled game day fails the primary for each venue shard and records the measured session gap for each venue. The published recovery targets equal the measured figures, and no document claims zero-gap failover.

notes: Split from the G p15 row. G p23 §27, not a raw item here, requires every critical component to have 'observable RTO/RPO or a documented reason exact guarantees cannot be promised'. Removed LIVE_CAPITAL.

title: Reflex never autoscales reactively during a market burst
statement: Reflex capacity must not be scaled reactively (autoscaled) during a market burst.
rationale: A burst is exactly when a new, cold, unbenchmarked VM would join the venue path, and when its start-up latency would hurt most.

sources.section: §18 Scaling and Performance Model — Reflex row ('no reactive autoscale during a market burst')

verification.check: No environment's plan attaches an autoscaler, a managed-instance-group autoscaling policy or a scale-out trigger to any Reflex VM.

notes: Split from the G p16 Reflex row; the positive scaling rule is REFLEX-054. G p4 §3, not a raw item here, contrasts Reflex with warm, data and AI components, which do autoscale.

title: Packages are fetched from Artifact Registry/GCS over a private channel
statement: The package manager must fetch packages from Artifact Registry or GCS, and verify them against KMS, over private HTTPS/gRPC and never over the public internet.
rationale: The package channel carries the node's whole decision input. A private path to the registry keeps both the fetch and the key lookup for verification off the public internet.

sources.section: §20 Critical Service-to-Service Connection Matrix — Package Manager to Artifact Registry/GCS + KMS verification (HTTPS/gRPC private)

verification.check: The Reflex host's network plan reaches Artifact Registry, GCS and KMS only through Private Google Access or Private Service Connect, and those private endpoints are the ones the package manager is configured to use.

notes: Split from the G p19 row; its 'KMS verification' is REFLEX-010 and its 'Warm' mode REFLEX-062. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept because ADR 0009 forbids an in-tree gRPC, TLS or Google auth client, and this channel needs all three unless the egress proxy carries it. P2 because GCP Phase 8 names the signed model package lifecycle. In-tree, policy and capital reach the cell over the mesh downlink (qip_edge::mesh::PolicyDownlink and CapitalDownlink), not from a registry.

title: The hot-path stages run in a fixed order, with risk before netting and execution
statement: Each event must pass through the node's stages in a fixed order: feed decode, order books, features, models, strategy, risk, netting, execution. No order may reach execution, and so the venue, without the local risk gate's approval for that order.
rationale: A fixed order makes every pass replayable and places the risk veto where nothing can route around it. An order that reaches the venue before risk has seen it is exactly the order the gate exists to stop.

sources.section: §21.1 Tick to order and learning — step 2 ('deterministic local risk gate approves/vetoes; order is sent directly to venue')
§02 Regional Cell — algorik-node pipeline ('Feed decode → books → features → models → strategy → risk → netting → execution')

verification.check: For generated event streams, every pass's journal shows the stages in the fixed order, and every order the venue adapter receives has an approve verdict for that order earlier in the same pass. Mutating the pipeline to skip the risk stage makes the check fail.

notes: Merges the two raw H L157 items, which quote the same pipeline, with the risk-then-send ordering of G p20 step 2. The gate's own properties are REFLEX-032 to REFLEX-034. The master's Lane 0 list (M p9), 'local risk, netting, routing', runs in the same order. In-tree, Cell::work runs signal to intent, feasibility, pricing, netting and crossing, decomposition, then dispatch, so feasibility also comes before netting. Neither blueprint says whether netted orders are checked again. Removed LIVE_CAPITAL and EXTERNAL_ACTION.

title: No proxy, mesh or gateway on Reflex traffic without benchmarked necessity
statement: Reflex traffic must not pass through a service mesh, proxy, Secure Web Proxy, Cloud NAT chain or general API gateway unless a benchmark shows that hop to be necessary.
rationale: Each hop adds latency and a component whose failure stops trading. On the venue path, a proxy must earn its place by measurement.

sources.section: §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'Routing Reflex traffic through service mesh, proxy, Secure Web Proxy, Cloud NAT chains or general API gateways without benchmarked necessity'

verification.check: In the plan, the routes from each Reflex host to its venues and peers contain no service-mesh, proxy, Secure Web Proxy, Cloud NAT or API-gateway hop, apart from any hop justified by a committed benchmark record.

notes: EXEC-030 holds the venue-side form. G p6's Host model bullet ('Avoid Kubernetes/service-mesh jitter') and G p5 §5 ('never inserted in Reflex path') say the same about the mesh. This conflicts with the in-tree design. The data-and-streaming rule puts the egress proxy (infrastructure/egress/envoy.yaml, run as a systemd unit beside the execution node under ADR 0024) in front of every vendor call, because the in-tree HTTP client speaks only plaintext. A real venue session through that proxy therefore needs the benchmark record this requirement asks for, or an ADR that changes one side or the other. No real venue exists today: QIP_VENUE_FEED accepts only simulated.
